newsitem.title: INDIA: India's rulers, Congress to start talks Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: India's rulers, Congress to start talks Wednesday.

text.p: India's ruling United Front coalition said on Tuesday that it would begin formal talks with the Congress party to try to resolve a political crisis.
United Front spokesman Jaipal Reddy told reporters that the coalition and Congress had agreed that formal talks would begin on Wednesday morning.

"Informal talks between leaders of the United Front and Congress have yielded an understanding to the effect that formal talks between representatives of the Congress party and the United Front will start from tomorrow morning," Reddy said.
Earlier on Tuesday, Congress party president Sitaram Kesri said he was willing to hold talks with Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's minority coalition, which faces a vote of confidence on Friday.
Kesri abruptly withdrew his party's support for Deve Gowda on March 30, triggering the political crisis which has jolted financial markets.

All-India Radio quoted Kesri as saying steps would be taken to ensure than India would not be forced into a mid-term poll, and a compromise between the ruling coalition and Congress appeared possible.
